correctness.rationale: All N Laplacian columns are affinely independent in the zero-sum hyperplane. Eigenvalues q (p-1), p (q-1), and N (1) give the exact Euclidean determinant volume. L-pseudoinverse columns give facet normals, and two orthogonal shore contrast spaces plus one block-contrast direction give exact facet areas. The relative area-factor error is O(1/N) uniformly; Stirling plus bounded x log x gives the uniform root-volume error even for p=1. Under r=a/(1-a), the exact derivative has sign g(r), with one zero because g decreases until sqrt(2)-1 then increases to zero at r=1. Compactness and uniform convergence give convergence of all integer maximizers. The actual checker constructed vertex-difference Gram determinants and verified all 44 p,q pairs for 3<=N<=10; six larger scans approach the claimed limiting fraction. Infinite conclusions follow from proof, not finite tests.
risks: No exact finite-N uniqueness is proved or asserted.
Floating-point enumeration and decimal constants are not infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: A graph Laplacian-column simplex has the same combinatorial type for every connected graph, but its inherited Euclidean boundary efficiency depends on spectral and inverse-spectral geometry. Comparing all complete-bipartite graphs of a fixed order is a natural constrained shape-optimization question. The theorem shows a counterintuitive macroscopic unbalanced global maximizer (smaller shore fraction about 0.1284), quantifies a 13.88% penalty relative to balance, treats stars uniformly, and provides exact finite facet spectra; this is a sharp geometric conclusion rather than a table entry or an arbitrary parameter slice.
risks: The theorem is restricted to complete bipartite graphs; it does not classify all connected graphs.
